questions.q: If conventional arrangements and/patterns are made more scarcer, other/arrangements and patterns will spring up. (SSC CHSL Tier-01 13/03/23)
o: Patterns are made more scarcer, other
Arrangements and patterns will spring up
questions.s: 'More scarcer' is a double comparative. 'Scarcer' is already the comparative form of 'scarce'.

questions.q:
There is few to be said on both sides.

[MTS 07/8/2019 S2]
questions.s: "Few" is for countable nouns, but the sentence refers to something uncountable. "Little" is correct.

questions.q:
The people in my office are smarter than other offices.

[MTS 05/8/2019 S2]
questions.s: The sentence compares people, not offices. The correct comparison is: "smarter than the people in other offices."

questions.q: This is (a) / the more interesting (b) / book I have read. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). For superlative, use 'most' instead of 'more.' Correct form is 'the most interesting.' Answer: (b). Superlative ke liye 'more' nahi, 'most' chahiye. Sahi form hai 'the most interesting.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: I am (a) / more lonelier (b) / here than I was in the USA. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Lonelier' is already comparative; 'more' is redundant. Correct form is 'lonelier.' Answer: (b). 'Lonelier' pehle se comparative hai, 'more' extra hai. Sahi form hai 'lonelier.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q:
Nowadays rent for a two room house can run as high to Rs. 40,000 in Mumbai.

[CHSL 01/07/2019 S3]
questions.s: as+ positive degree+as

questions.q: The wedding reception will be hosted in Mumbai at a late date.
questions.s:
Explanation:- (c) use ‘later’ instead of ‘late’

Late - (happening or being) near the end of a period of time:

Later - at a time in the future or after the time you have mentioned:

questions.q:
He was enough tall / to be admitted / into the armed forces.

[CPO 10/11/2022 S3]
questions.s: The correct phrase is "tall enough" (adjective + enough) instead of "enough tall.”

questions.q: Although the patient (a) was rudely with the (b)/ nurses, he behaved nicely with the doctor. (d) No Error
questions.s: Use "was rude with" (adjective) not "rudely with" (adverb).

questions.q: It was really surprising / that the two bosom friends fought / over such a triviale matter / and stopped all communications with each other.
o: and stopped all communications with each other
questions.s:
Explanation:- (a) use ‘trivial’ instead of ‘triviale’ because the correct word is trivial which means having little value or importance:

Note:- Is type ke spelling based error waise toh kam aate hain lekin kabhi kabhi aa jaate hain.

questions.q: No less than thousands of spectators are/ waiting for Dhoni to come out/ in the field and play his / masterful stroke.
o: No less than thousands of spectators are
questions.s: Explanation:- Use fewer in place of less. Kyunki 'no less than' is phrase ka use uncountable cheezon ke liye hota hai aur 'no fewer than' is phrase ka use countable cheezon ke liye hota hai. Aage likha thousands of spectators se pata chal rha hai ki veh countable hai plural hai isliye 'no fewer than' ka use hoga.

questions.q:
Direction: Improve the bold part in each of the following sentences, if needed.

He found a wooden broken chair in the room.
o: wooden and broken chair
broken wooden chair
broken and wooden chair
No improvement
questions.s: 'wooden broken chair' के बदले 'broken wooden chair का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि Adjective of Marterial का प्रयोग अपने Noun के पहले होता है और Adjective of Material के पहले अन्य Adjectives का;

questions.q: Simplest solution (a) than this expensive (b) method which we are suggesting (c) should be found out. (d)/ No Error (e)
questions.s: Use comparative: "A simpler solution than this expensive method...".

questions.q: A journey by car is (a)/ as quick or perhaps quicker (b)/ than the one by train. (c)/ in this particular case (d)/ No Error (e)
questions.s: Should be "as quick as, or perhaps quicker than".

questions.q: Mango, the most unique fruit (a) / is available in India (b) / in plenty/ (c)/ No error (d)
questions.s: "Unique" does not take degree; just "a unique fruit".

questions.q:
A study finds that the average staff cost at/a public sector bank is high than that at/its private sector counterpart.

(SSC CHSL Tier-01 09/03/23)
o: A public sector bank is high than that at
A study finds that the average staff cost at
questions.s: "is high than" is incorrect. The correct form should be "is higher than" because "higher" is the correct comparative form of "high.”

questions.q:
In the five next/years, the migration/will surely stop.

[SSC CHSL Tier-01 09/03/23]
questions.s: "In the next five years" instead of "In the five next years."

questions.q:
Ashoka was one of the greater king of India.

{CHSL 9/8/2021 S3}
questions.s: The sentence is referring to Ashoka being one of the most outstanding kings in India, so the superlative form "the greatest" is required.

questions.q: She is (a) / more smarter (b) / than her cousin. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Smarter' is already comparative; 'more' is redundant. Correct form is 'smarter than.' Answer: (b). 'Smarter' pehle se comparative hai, 'more' extra hai. Sahi form hai 'smarter than.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: The car flew off the road (a)/ and fell into the valley (b)/ because Amit was driving faster. (d)/ No error (e)
o: The car flew off the road
questions.s: Comparative "faster" is incomplete without comparison. Use "too fast" to show excessive speed causing accident.

questions.q: It is unlikely that you will (a)/ find more qualified and experience (b)/ candidate than Mr. Prasad (c)/ for the post of president. (d)/ No error (e)
o: It is unlikely that you will
questions.s: Use "qualified and experienced candidate" - both should be past participles.

questions.q: The man is (1)/ the most tallest (2)/ of the group (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.s: Tallest” is already a superlative degree, so adding most creates a double superlative, which is incorrect.

questions.q: My All students passed the exam with flying colors.
questions.s:
" Possessive case comes after ‘All’ and ‘Both’ and not before them. The correct option is (c) "My All students.

The corrected sentence should be: "All my students passed the exam with flying colors."

questions.q: But for your help (a) / no boys would have (b) / succeeded in an (c) / All India competition like this. (d) / No error (e)
questions.s: It should be "in an All-India competition"; hyphenated adjective.
